# Independent noise-biome reference fixtures

`surface.csv` contains 5,880 quart-height samples generated by
`surface-reference.c` against cubiomes commit
`e61f90580cbdd883214a8054670dacae655e59c0`, using GCC 16.2.0
`-std=c11 -O3 -fwrapv -ffp-contract=off`. Link `generator.c biomenoise.c
noise.c layers.c biomes.c -lm`. Versions 1.18.2, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, normal/large
biomes, five signed seeds and four 7×7 grids include negative coordinates and
the world border. 5,877 samples are bit-identical; three differ by one depth
quantization unit (at most 0.013157 blocks) because C rearranges the float spline
offset while Go preserves Minecraft's density graph. This is the same existing
depth tolerance used for climate reference tests; it is not a heightmap oracle
for Minecraft's generated terrain. 26.3 additionally compares the surface path
with its separately validated native Climate pipeline, not this older C release.
`TestSurfaceRangeMatchesScalar` checks variable-height Voronoi, TerraBlender
tree histories and negative-coordinate interpolation against uncached queries.
`TestSurfaceCustomGraphAndReseed` checks datapack depth/3D-noise changes and seed
rebinding. Go tests require neither a C compiler nor a JVM.

`terrablender-registration-1.20.1.json.gz` records 10,000 results from the actual
Minecraft 1.20.1 `Climate.ParameterList` using the original YUNG's Cave Biomes
2.0.5 / TerraBlender 3.0.1.10 source-generated parameters. The first 7,595 queries
alternate parameter-box endpoints; remaining queries use Java Random seed
`0x5eed` and signed values in [-12000, 12000]. Query order preserves previous-leaf
history and tests tie handling. The ordinary Go test needs neither a JAR nor Java.
The [provenance file](../data/terrablender-1.20.1.provenance.json) records hashes
and the independent source-compilation procedure.

`cubiomes.json` and `noise.json` were produced by the C programs in this directory,
compiled against [cubiomes commit e61f90580cbdd883214a8054670dacae655e59c0](https://github.com/Cubitect/cubiomes/tree/e61f90580cbdd883214a8054670dacae655e59c0).
They were not generated by the Go implementation under test. Cubiomes is MIT
licensed; see `../data/LICENSE-cubiomes.txt`.

From that cubiomes checkout, with these two generators copied into it:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 reference.c biomenoise.c noise.c layers.c biomes.c -lm -o reference
./reference > cubiomes.json
cc -std=c11 -O2 noise-reference.c noise.c -lm -o noise-reference
./noise-reference > noise.json
```

The checked-in outputs were generated using MSVC 2022 `cl /std:c11 /O2
/fp:precise` on Windows. Do not enable fast-math. Copy outputs back here and run
`go test ./cubiomes ./internal/launcher -run 'TestClimateCubiomesReference|TestNoiseCubiomesReference'`.
No C compiler or JVM is needed to run the Go tests or launcher.

## Historical version fixtures and performance comparisons

`legacy-reference.c` generates `legacy.json` with GCC 16.2.0 on Windows x64,
using `-std=c11 -O3 -fwrapv -ffp-contract=off` and the same pinned revision.
Link `generator.c biomenoise.c noise.c layers.c biomes.c -lm`. It covers
21 version profiles (Beta 1.7/1.8 and 1.0–1.17, including both 1.16 variants),
seven seeds including signed extremes, available dimensions and large biomes.
There are 539 combinations, 68,992 point IDs and 19,739,258 raster IDs checked
by whole-raster FNV-1a hashes. Points exercise negative and far coordinates;
grids exercise odd sizes, negative offsets and 1:4/1:1 scales.

Two explicit reference choices matter:

- Beta 1.7 uses `NO_BETA_OCEAN`, sampling climate rather than the experimental
  sea-level terrain estimate. This is also the Go library's documented mode.
- For 1.15+ block queries the reference composes `voronoiAccess3D` with quart
  generation. The pinned `mapVoronoiPlane` helper uses different Y seeds and
  fixed vertical distances; its `mapVoronoi` wrapper also offsets X/Z twice.
  The tests use the documented 3D access primitive, preserving actual Y.

`benchmark.c --hashes` generates `benchmark-hashes.json`, independently from
Go, for the eleven timed workloads. Legacy generations use `genBiomes`;
modern Overworld calls `sampleBiomeNoise` in raster order with previous-leaf
history and normal coordinate shifts, matching Go `GenerateIDs` semantics.
Upstream `genBiomes(scale=4)` instead starts a fresh tree search for every cell;
the difference can affect boundary ties. No C library source is modified.
The modern Nether is excluded from the equal-output comparison because its
Go implementation follows the modern quantized integer-distance lookup while
this upstream C revision uses the old floating-point distance rule.

See [`../BENCHMARKS.md`](../BENCHMARKS.md) for results, limitations and the
cross-platform reproduction script. Checked-in fixtures let ordinary Go tests
run without GCC or network access.

`end.json` adds 154 End biome records (seven seeds, 22 block-coordinate pairs),
covering all five End biomes, negative chunk boundaries and far-End NaN rings.
`end-reference.c` uses the same pinned upstream cubiomes `setEndSeed` and
`mapEndBiome`, compiled with the same MSVC flags:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 end-reference.c biomenoise.c noise.c layers.c biomes.c -lm -o end-reference
./end-reference > end.json
```

Run `go test ./internal/launcher -run TestEndCubiomesReference`. A separate
analytic assertion preserves vanilla's positive int-overflow corner at block
(1048576, −1048576): the squared radial argument wraps to 2, giving clamped
height 80 and End highlands. Cubiomes' optimized `mapEndBiome` omits that tiny
positive-overflow island; its fixtures deliberately use a nearby NaN ring
instead. The implementation follows vanilla's
[EndIslandDensityFunction](https://github.com/mahtomedi/minecraft/blob/main/src/main/java/net/minecraft/world/level/levelgen/DensityFunctions.java)
for the overflow behavior and
[TheEndBiomeSource](https://github.com/mahtomedi/minecraft/blob/main/src/main/java/net/minecraft/world/level/biome/TheEndBiomeSource.java)
for erosion thresholds.

`cubiomes-pale.json` adds 18 targeted coordinate records for 1.21.4, 1.21.5 and
1.21.11, both changed dark-forest/pale-garden locations and unchanged pale
gardens, using three seeds. It uses the pinned [PR #162 fork](https://github.com/Zes-MinKey-Young/cubiomes/tree/ca9fcb4e2b4f29a88b15a19fe1f00a73bf503ec2)
and `pale-reference.c`. From that checkout, compile and run:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 pale-reference.c biomenoise.c noise.c layers.c biomes.c -lm -o pale-reference
./pale-reference > cubiomes-pale.json
```

Together the fixtures assert 792 biome IDs. In particular, seed 0 at
(-4608,128,7104) is dark forest in 1.21.4 and pale garden in 1.21.5/1.21.11.
The fork's tree changes come from the vanilla data report; it is an unmerged
upstream contribution, and its provenance is documented in the data README.

The main file has 378 coordinate records, each containing Overworld and Nether results:
1.18.2, 1.19.2, 1.19.4, 1.20.1, 1.21.4, plus 1.20.1 large biomes. Seeds are
0, 1, 42, 123456789, −1, MinInt64 and MaxInt64. Coordinates include origin,
negative quart boundaries, underground/elevated slices and the world-border
region. As one readily inspectable example, 1.20.1 seed 0 at block (0,64,0)
has noise biome `minecraft:river`; the fixture also records all six climate
components, so a plausible-looking wrong map cannot pass.

Coordinates are converted by arithmetic shift to quart coordinates, with a
fresh tree search for each reference query. These are noise biomes, before
block Voronoi zoom, not an exact F3 biome claim at every boundary. Cubiomes
rearranges the depth spline/y arithmetic slightly; the climate assertion permits
one quantized unit (0.0001) for depth only. Every biome ID and other climate
component must match exactly. Tests separately cover previous-leaf tie behavior.

`noise.json` checks four raw outputs for each seeded RNG and one ImprovedNoise
and NormalNoise evaluation, for four extreme/ordinary seeds and both random
algorithms. Modern NormalNoise uses amplitudes `[1,0,0.5,1]` to exercise skipped
and weighted octaves; legacy NormalNoise uses the Nether-compatible path.

`voronoi.json` adds 1,792 queries from `voronoi-reference.c`, using the same pinned
upstream `getVoronoiSHA` and `voronoiAccess3D`. Seven seeds include both signed
extremes. Each seed has 128 near-origin negative/quart-boundary coordinates and
128 deterministic scattered positions within ±30,000,000 blocks, with heights
between −2048 and 2047. Both the SHA seed and all three selected quart coordinates
must match exactly. The fixture was generated with MSVC `/std:c11 /O2 /fp:precise`:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 -fwrapv voronoi-reference.c layers.c noise.c biomes.c -lm -o voronoi-reference
./voronoi-reference > voronoi.json
go test ./cubiomes -run TestVoronoiCubiomesReference
```
